title: Optimistic cache lookup and safe rollback for embeddings endpoint
creator: Ava Chen
description: Improve embeddings endpoint latency and scaling by introducing an optimistic cache lookup path for prefix and content-hash keys, with a deterministic rollback strategy when cache validation fails. This ticket captures the engineering design, implementation tasks, and rollout for a safe, observable caching layer that deduplicates work while preserving reranking quality.
background: We currently compute embeddings on every request when prefixes or recent content overlap. Prior efforts increased hit rates using dedupe heuristics, but some workloads still incur redundant compute and high p95 latency under bursty traffic. Reranking customers are sensitive to even small quality regressions; staleness or hash collisions are unacceptable. We need a bold optimization that serves cached vectors optimistically to reduce latency while ensuring exactness or controlled fallback when validation fails.
proposed_solution: 1) Add an optimistic lookup phase: check a compact deterministic prefix index + content-hash (SHA256 truncated) to return a cached embedding immediately if positive. 2) Perform an asynchronous strong-validate step: compute a lightweight checksum of the source input on the compute path and compare; if validation fails, issue a rollback: mark response as stale and re-run embedding generation synchronously for the requester and update cache atomically. 3) Introduce versioned cache entries with monotonic generation IDs so rollbacks can detect races. 4) Use per-tenant TTL cohorts and probabilistic bloom filters to reduce unnecessary backend lookups. 5) Expose metrics and gating to avoid returning optimistic results to high-sensitivity reranking routes until validated by canary.
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency for embeddings endpoint reduced by >= 18% on production-like load with default cache configs
Cache hit rate for repeated prefixes improved to >= 65% in synthetic prefix-heavy workloads
No measurable degradation in reranking quality: NDCG@10 drop <= 0.5% vs baseline across standard evals
Rollback correctness: 100% of validation failures trigger synchronous recompute and cache patching; no stale vector observed in post-validated route
Feature gated behind runtime flag and can be disabled per-tenant via config
performance_targets: Avg token compute reduction per request: target 12%-25% depending on workload
End-to-end p99 impact: <= +5% compared to current baseline (i.e., avoid tail regressions)
Atomic cache write latency: < 10ms median for in-memory cache paths
rollout_plan: Implement feature behind a runtime flag and per-route config (start in dev).
Unit and integration tests + microbenchmark in CI to validate race-free rollback semantics.
Canary: enable for 1% of traffic (non-reranking, low-sensitivity tenants) for 48h and monitor metrics.
Expand to 10% for another 48h; run regression evals against production traffic snapshots.
Enable on reranking routes but with strict validation (no optimistic returns) for 2 weeks; then gradually remove strict validation if metrics are stable.
Full rollout by tenant cohorts with opt-out in Console within release window.
test_plan: Unit tests for optimistic lookup + rollback state machine (edge cases: concurrent writes, partial failures).
Integration test that simulates hash collision and ensures rollback leads to recompute and correct replacement in cache.
Load test with synthetic prefix-heavy traffic to measure hit rates and latency improvements.
Quality regression test suite: run NDCG and retrieval-based evals on reranking models before and after enabling feature.
Chaos test: simulate cache store flaps and ensure fallback paths are robust and do not deadlock callers.
monitoring_and_alerts: Metric: optimistic_validation_failure_rate -> alert if > 1% sustained over 5m on production routes
Dashboard: hit-rate heatmap by prefix length, tenant, and time-of-day
Alert: reranking_quality_regression if NDCG drop > 0.7% on production eval set post-deploy
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: returning expired or incorrect embeddings could silently degrade downstream reranking. Mitigation: strict validation for high-sensitivity routes and canary gating; strong post-deploy audit logs for returned optimistic responses.

Risk: hash collisions causing erroneous cache hits. Mitigation: use 256-bit SHA truncated to 120 bits for compact keys and perform checksum compare; on collision detection always recompute and bump collision counter.
Risk: race between concurrent writes causing stale overwrite. Mitigation: use generation IDs and compare-and-set semantics on cache writes; instrument cases where CAS fails and trigger retry.

Risk: increased complexity in cache invalidation. Mitigation: model a small, deterministic set of invalidation policies (time-based TTLs per cohort, explicit eviction on model updates, and tenant-scoped purge endpoints).
